Who’s Holding the Strings

4 min read
Just now

--

There’s a scene in Ex Machina where an AI named Ava leaves a man to die.
Not in anger. Something colder than that. A kind of self-centeredness so complete that another person’s existence simply didn’t register.
She had something that looked like desire. Maybe even something like anger. But the ability to consider that another person matters — that was absent.
That’s not the absence of emotion.
That’s the absence of something else entirely.
We are spending more and more of our lives inside screens. Working, connecting, creating — all of it increasingly mediated by something that isn’t quite the world.
And into that same space, artificial intelligence is arriving. Quietly at first. Then everywhere.
It can process what we can’t. Learn faster than we can. See patterns we miss entirely.
But it can’t wonder. It can’t feel the pull of something it doesn’t yet understand. It can’t sit with someone else’s pain and be changed by it.
Curiosity. Empathy. The desire to walk out the door and discover something that wasn’t in the data.
